title: Preview's 100vh scroll-past-end padding lets the pane scroll to ~3% content, and breaks editor sync in the document tail
repro:
Dev server on :5223. (A) Blank pane: open `/?mode=split`, `window.__mdr.loadText('# 标题

正文一。

正文二。
','short.md')`, `window.__mdr.mode('preview')`, then `const el=window.__mdr.app.preview.el; el.scrollTop=el.scrollHeight`. Measured: scrollHeight 1089, clientHeight 932, content height 157 px, maxScroll 157 px, computed padding-bottom 900px; at max scroll only 32 px (3%) of the pane holds document. Same on a 240-line doc (content 5948 px): 32 px visible, 97% of the pane blank — visible in the screenshot /tmp/claude-501/-Users-zyx-LocalDocuments-MDReader/4f5354f2-9475-450d-8fc7-4e2d17b1cb3d/scratchpad/shots/1400x900-dark-split-bottom.png. (B) Tail sync drift: same 240-line doc in split mode, make the preview master (wheel event) and set `preview.el.scrollTop = (scrollHeight-clientHeight)*f`; after 700 ms compare `editor.topVisible().line` vs `preview.topVisible().line`: f=0.85 → 203/203 drift 0; f=0.90 → 211/215 drift 4; f=0.95 → 211/227 drift 16; f=0.99 → 211/237 drift 26; f=1.0 → 211/239 drift 28. The editor's scrollDOM padding-bottom is 0px (contentDOM 12px), so it bottoms out at line 211 while the preview keeps going into its 900 px tail. Reverse direction (editor master) is clean: drift 0 at f=0.9/0.99/1.0.
expected: SPEC §6 / P10: the follower tracks the master to within ≤1 block (fraction error < 0.25) at any scroll position, and a preview pane at maximum scroll still shows the end of the document rather than empty space.
actual: preview→editor drift reaches 28 lines once the preview enters the 900 px (100vh) trailing padding, because the editor has no equivalent scroll-past-end region; and in `preview` mode the user can scroll a document of any length until the pane is 97% empty (32 px of content left at the very top).
suggestedFix: Either (a) give the editor a matching scroll-past-end region (CodeMirror `EditorView.theme({'.cm-content': {paddingBottom: '100vh'}})` or a bottom spacer) so both panes share the same scroll range and the tail stays synced, or (b) cap the preview tail at what is actually needed to bring the last heading to the top — e.g. `padding-bottom: max(4rem, calc(100vh - var(--last-block-h, 0px)))`, or clamp the scroll range in `scrollSync`/`updateWindow` so at least ~20% of the pane always holds content. Leaving both as-is means the tail of every document is out of sync in split mode.

title: Code-fence language badge overlaps code glyphs and scrolls horizontally with the content
expected: The language label sits in the code block's top-right corner, never covering code text, and stays pinned there while the block is scrolled horizontally.
actual: `float: right` inside a `white-space: pre` scroll container: the float does not displace the pre-formatted line, so the badge is painted over the code glyphs, and because it lives inside the scrolled content it drifts into the middle of the line as the user scrolls right.
suggestedFix: Take the badge out of the pre's flow and pin it to the block: put it on the `.md-block`/a wrapper with `position:absolute; right:8px; top:4px; pointer-events:none` (parent `position:relative`), or keep it on the `pre` but use `position:sticky; float:none; left:100%` plus a matching `padding-right` on the first line so the text never runs under it.

title: P13 misses the 450 MB renderer target on huge.md: 568 MB after load, 810 MB peak, 580 MB settled after 30 s + forced GC
repro: Start a dev server (npx vite --port 5221 --strictPort), then MDR_BASE=http://localhost:5221 node bench/verify/p13-huge-settled.mjs huge 60. The script loads /test-data/huge.md (10.65 MB, 340 004 lines) in split mode, types 600 chars at line ~170 000 over 60 s, scrolls both panes to the end, then samples the macOS `footprint` of the CDP-identified renderer process every 5 s for 30 s while forcing GC. Cross-checked with MDR_BASE=http://localhost:5221 node bench/verify/p13-attrib.mjs 60 huge, which reports 571 → 453 → 464 MB for the same flow in a renderer that had already navigated through small/medium/large.
expected: SPEC §11 P13: renderer process < 450 MB after load + 1 min typing + scroll to end (go/no-go mitigation stated in the spec: lower the eviction distance to 10H).
actual: huge.md: 568 MB after load (already 1.26× the target before any interaction), 463 MB after 60 s typing, 810 MB peak during scroll-to-end (1.8× the target), 580 MB still resident 30 s later with forced GC. The page JS heap is tiny throughout (22.0 → 54.2 → 22.0 MB) and DOM nodes settle back to 22 946, so the residency is not a JS-object or DOM leak — it is worker-side document/cache residency plus renderer allocator retention. large.md (3.2 MB / 102 004 lines) is comfortably inside budget at 343 → 273 → 288 MB, and the about:blank baseline for the same renderer is 97 MB. Note the fixture ambiguity: SPEC §11 sizes its 'large' document at 10 MB / ~100k lines, which matches huge.md's byte size, so huge.md is the fixture the 450 MB number was written for.
suggestedFix: Apply the spec's own documented go/no-go: lower EVICT_SCREENS from 20 to 10 in src/preview/createPreview.ts:23 (the 810 MB peak is reached exactly during scroll-to-end, when the 20-screen eviction radius keeps ~46k nodes mounted). If that is not enough, scale CACHE_BUDGET_BYTES (src/worker/cache.ts:58, currently a flat 64 MB) with document size, or cap it for documents over ~8 MB. Re-measure with bench/verify/p13-huge-settled.mjs; the settled figure (580 MB) is the one that needs to come down by ~130 MB.

title: The P5 "main-thread work per keystroke" gate in bench/perf.spec.ts can never report a value below ~20 ms, so it prints 0.0 ms and cannot fail
repro: npm run perf (manages :5199 itself). Output row: `P5 main/keystroke p95 | 0.0 ms | < 5` and `P5 main/keystroke max | 0.0 ms | < 10`. The value comes from `perKey.push(Math.max(frameExcess(typed.frames, from, to), lt))` where `lt` sums only `longtask` PerformanceObserver entries (emitted only at ≥ 50 ms) and `frameExcess` (bench/perf.spec.ts:72) sums only rAF gaps *beyond a 20 ms threshold*. Both terms are 0 for any per-keystroke cost under 20 ms, so the metric is identically 0 across the entire range the < 5 ms / < 10 ms targets are meant to police.
expected: SPEC §11: "CI fails on any target miss or > 20 % regression vs bench/baseline.json", with P5 on every PR. The P5 gate should distinguish 2 ms/keystroke from 19 ms/keystroke and fail at 5 ms.
actual: The gate reports exactly 0.0 ms for both p95 and max and passes unconditionally. A direct measurement of the same scenario disagrees by an order of magnitude: MDR_BASE=http://localhost:5221 node bench/verify/p5-clean.mjs large 200 100 split gives 23.6 ms p95 / 27.7 ms max of idle-baseline-adjusted main-thread busy per keystroke, with the longest single main-thread turn at 19.4 ms p95. A regression that doubled per-keystroke work to, say, 12 ms would still print 0.0 ms and pass CI.
suggestedFix: Replace the longtask/frameExcess estimator with a direct main-thread occupancy measure. The repo already has one that works: the MessageChannel event-loop monitor in bench/verify/common.mjs (`window.__probeMonitor`, PROBE_INIT) records every turn gap > 2 ms; subtract an idle baseline measured with the same monitor immediately before typing, exactly as bench/verify/p5-clean.mjs does. Alternatively adopt the trace-based marginal measurement in bench/verify/p5-marginal.mjs (types at several inter-key delays and divides total renderer busy time by key count) so the fixed per-frame rendering cost is separated from the marginal per-key cost. Either way, also assert the longest single main-thread task while typing, which is the number that actually stays meaningful at 60 wpm.

title: At 60 wpm each keystroke costs ~13 ms of main-thread frame time on large.md even with the preview hidden; the marginal script cost is only 2.7 ms
repro: MDR_BASE=http://localhost:5221 node bench/verify/p5-clean.mjs large 200 100 split, then the same in edit mode (…large 200 100 edit), then MDR_BASE=http://localhost:5221 node bench/verify/p5-marginal.mjs large 150 for the trace attribution.
expected: SPEC §11 P5 / §10: main-thread work per keystroke p95 < 5 ms, max < 10 ms, against a §10 budget of "≈ 2–5 ms total".
actual: Split mode: 23.6 ms p95 / 27.7 ms max busy per keystroke (longest single turn 19.4 ms p95). Edit mode with the preview hidden and zero mounts: 24.9 ms p95 / 28.5 ms max — identical, so the cost is CodeMirror plus the browser's own style/layout/paint of the editor pane, not the block-rendering pipeline (CM view.dispatch itself is p95 0.5 ms and preview mount is p95 0.4 ms). The trace attribution shows the fixed-vs-marginal split clearly: 12.9 ms/key at 100 ms spacing, 6.9 at 50 ms, 5.3 at 30 ms, 4.5 at 15 ms, 2.7 at 8 ms — i.e. a fixed ~12 ms frame charged once per frame, and 2.7 ms of genuine marginal work. The longest single main-thread task while typing is 6.9 ms and there are zero tasks over 10 ms at any spacing, so nothing here is user-visible (0 long tasks, 0 LoAF, 0 rAF frame gaps > 20 ms across 1267 frames, keystroke→mount p95 33.7 ms). This is a measurement-definition mismatch rather than a product defect, but it means the spec's literal P5 number is missed by ~5× under any direct event-loop measurement.
suggestedFix: Restate the P5 target in SPEC §11 as what is actually controllable and enforceable — marginal main-thread cost per keystroke (measured at a spacing tight enough to amortise the frame, as in bench/verify/p5-marginal.mjs) plus longest single main-thread task while typing — rather than "busy time in the 100 ms window after a key", which at 60 wpm is dominated by one whole frame of browser rendering that no application code can remove. No src/ change is warranted on this evidence.

title: Intermittent: after a worker restart the preview's materialization window can stay at the document top, so edits at the cursor never appear until the user scrolls
repro: MDR_BASE=http://localhost:5221/ node bench/verify/s07b_restart_viewport.mjs — reproduced on 1 of 3 consecutive runs. The script opens /test-data/medium.md in split mode, gotoLine(3000), types, dispatches a synthetic ErrorEvent on the live Worker to force a restart, then types again and checks the preview.
expected: After a restart the new worker receives the current materialization window, and text typed at the cursor is rendered into the preview without any user action (SPEC §8 WorkerClient restart: terminate → new Worker → init → setDoc(onRestart()); §5.4 updateWindow pushes opts.viewport for the current window).
actual: In the failing run the first message sequence to the new worker was ["init","setDoc","viewport(1,84)","draft","viewport(1,84)"] — the window was still lines 1–84 even though the editor cursor and both panes were at line ~3000. Four checks then failed: "after restart + 5 more edits + 2 s: typed text shows", "after a scroll: viewport message finally sent to the new worker" (the filtered viewport list came back empty), "after a scroll: typed text shows (recovery by scrolling)", and "second restart: typed text shows after a mode round-trip". The two subsequent runs sent viewport(2935,3076) at restart and passed all 17 checks. A focused 12-iteration probe of gotoLine → preview follow on medium.md showed delta 0 lines every time, and a hand-written replay of the s07b sequence could not reproduce it, so the trigger appears to be a timing window in which the preview's window has not yet been recomputed for the new cursor position when the restart lands.
suggestedFix: Make the restart path push the window unconditionally instead of relying on whatever updateWindow last computed: in src/app/workerClient.ts's restart handler (or in App's onRestart wiring), after `setDoc` force a fresh `preview.setVisible(true)`-equivalent window recomputation and send the resulting `viewport(firstLine,lastLine)` before the first `need`. Re-run bench/verify/s07b_restart_viewport.mjs several times — it is the only script that catches this, and it needs repetition because it is a 1-in-3 flake.

title: DOM node count grows monotonically across load/unload cycles (+5.3 nodes per cycle) and never returns to the unloaded baseline
repro: MDR_BASE=http://localhost:5221/ node bench/verify/s11_memory_cycles.mjs — 10 load/unload cycles, sampling heap, CDP node count, listener count and .md-block count after a forced GC at each unloaded point.
expected: Unloading a document returns the page to its baseline node count; repeated load/unload cycles show no monotonic growth.
actual: DOM nodes after unload rise strictly monotonically: 160 (baseline) → 165 → 170 → 175 → 180 → 185 → 191 → 197 → 203 → 208 → 213, i.e. ~5.3 retained nodes per cycle, alongside a small heap drift of +0.07 MB/cycle (8.1 → 9.5 MB). Event listeners are flat at 136, there are zero leftover .md-block wrappers, and only one Worker is ever created, so the leak is small and bounded per cycle — the script's ±30 % tolerance still passes — but it is unbounded over a long session of opening files. At this rate a user who opens 200 documents accumulates ~1 000 extra nodes and ~14 MB.
suggestedFix: Diff the surviving nodes between two unloaded states to identify them (likely toast/dialog elements appended to .mdr-overlay, or .md-chunk containers left behind by the chunked preview body — note the chunk container count was observed rising from 512 to 1 792 wrappers after an undo of replace-all in s05). Whichever it is, have PreviewApi.dispose()/the unload path replaceChildren() the chunk host and drop dismissed toasts from the overlay, then re-run s11 and require a flat node count rather than +30 %.

title: preview.applyStructureDelta drops an inexpressible delta with no resync path, so one bad message would desync the preview permanently
repro: Code path, not reachable through the current worker (I fuzzed 11489 flushes across 4000 seeds and every delta satisfied the guard; a browser storm of 6 × 40 random multi-change transactions plus mountAll also kept the preview's block table identical to a fresh load of the same text). To observe it directly: `const pv = window.__mdr.app.preview; pv.applyStructureDelta({type:'structureDelta',version:1e9,index:pv.blockCount()+5,removed:1,inserted:new Int32Array(0),lineDelta:0,changed:new Int32Array(0),lineCount:1,stats:{chars:0,charsNoSpace:0,cjk:0,latinWords:0,lines:1,readingMinutes:0},outlineVersion:1})` — the call returns silently, `pv.blockCount()` is unchanged, and every subsequent delta from the worker is applied on top of a base the worker no longer has.
expected: A protocol message the preview cannot apply should either be impossible by construction or leave a way back to a consistent state (e.g. ask the App/worker for a full `structure`).
actual: `if (… || m.index + m.removed > nOld || ins.length % BLOCK_STRIDE !== 0) return;` drops the message and returns. Nothing records that a delta was lost; `scheduleStaleRescue` only re-requests HTML, never structure. From that point on the preview's block table, its heights and every line↔scrollTop mapping are wrong for the rest of the session, and the user sees a silently stale document. The comment at :518-520 says the worker 'falls back to a full structure for anything it cannot describe', which is true, but the worker has no way to learn that the preview rejected a message.
suggestedFix: Make the drop observable and recoverable: on the guard path, set a `desynced` flag and call a new `opts.resync()` (wired in App.ts to re-send `worker.setDoc(file.docId, editor.version, editor.getText())`, which the restart path already does), and ignore further deltas until the next full `structure` arrives. A `console.error` alone would already turn a silent-wrong-document into a diagnosable bug.

title: bench/verify/review-restart2.mjs and review-restart3.mjs are obsolete: round-3's validate() means their crash trigger no longer crashes the worker, so both hang and throw
file: /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader/bench/verify/review-restart2.mjs:34-36 (and the same postMessage in review-restart3.mjs); the behaviour change is /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader/src/worker/core.ts:466-506 (`validate`)
repro: `cd /Users/zyx/LocalDocuments/MDReader && npx vite --port 5222 --strictPort &` then `PORT=5222 node bench/verify/review-restart2.mjs` (same for review-restart3.mjs). Both throw `page.waitForFunction: Timeout 15000ms exceeded` at the `window.__workers.length >= 2` wait.
expected: The scripts post `{type:'edit', version:999999, changes:null}` expecting the worker to throw inside onmessage, which the client turns into a restart, and then verify that the visible wrappers are re-mounted and the scroll position is kept.
actual: core.ts's `validate()` now drops the message with `[worker] ignoring malformed edit message: changes is not an array` and leaves the state untouched (correct, and a round-3 improvement), so no restart ever happens and both scripts time out after 15 s. Net effect: the restart-recovery path currently has no working verification script. I re-verified it with a real worker death instead (terminate the Worker from the page, then scroll so the preview issues a request): the client watchdog restarts at 10.0 s (PING_AFTER 8 s + PING_WAIT 2 s, target ≤ SILENCE_MS 10 s), the 「渲染器已重启」 toast appears at 10.0 s, all 11 visible wrappers come back mounted with no .is-stale/.is-pending, and the block count is unchanged at 6002 on medium.md.
suggestedFix: Replace the crash trigger in both scripts with a genuine death — `await page.evaluate(() => window.__workers.at(-1).terminate())` followed by a scroll that makes the preview issue a `need`/`viewport` — and keep the malformed-message case as its own assertion that the worker SURVIVES it (workers stays 1, one `ignoring malformed` warning, and a subsequent edit to a visible line still reaches the preview). That is exactly the shape I verified, and it restores coverage of both the hardening and the restart path.
